comment: Pinned input of the wimboot build (build/wimboot/wimbootsrc.py): iPXE's wimboot release tag as GitHub's source archive. The archive is checked against its SHA-256 and size before use, and its embedded commit id against 'commit'. To update: new tag, url, sha256, size, commit, source_date_epoch; then check that every patch in patches/series still applies (the build fails otherwise).
name: wimboot
source_date_epoch_comment: 2025-11-17T23:58:15Z, the publication time of the v2.9.0 release: file times of the output
prebuilt_comment: binaries committed in the upstream tree; deleted before the build so nothing prebuilt can reach the output
target_comment: the x86_64 hybrid image: a bzImage header for BIOS (GRUB linux16, wimboot's own 16/32-bit code) plus a PE32+ EFI entry point for 64-bit UEFI - one file for both (upstream ships the same image as 'wimboot'). The make target that copies it to 'wimboot.x86_64' also compares pesign hashes; we skip it (no pesign, nothing is signed)

upstream_release_binary.comment: informational only: upstream's own x86_64 binary (in-tree src/wimboot.x86_64, unpatched, upstream toolchain) and the Microsoft-signed release asset. Neither is shipped; our patched build differs from both

docker_comment: the docker builder uses GRUB's pinned image and apt snapshot (build/grub/source.lock.json 'docker') with these packages
